name: Italy
snapshot: Giorgia Meloni lost her first big vote when Italians rejected her judicial reform in a March 2026 referendum, setting up a tense run to the 2027 election.
culture: Italy holds more UNESCO World Heritage sites than almost any other country, from Rome and Florence to Venice and Pompeii. Its food, opera, fashion and design are global benchmarks. Regional identity is strong, with dialects and cuisines changing from town to town. Football, especially Serie A, and the Catholic Church shape national life.
society: Italy has one of the world's oldest populations and one of the lowest birth rates, and many young people emigrate. The north is industrial and rich, the south poorer. Public debt is around 135 percent of GDP. Migration across the Mediterranean is a political flashpoint, and Meloni's government has tried to process asylum seekers in Albania.

story: Italy has had nearly 70 governments since 1946, and its prime ministers usually last about a year. Giorgia Meloni, the first woman to hold the job and leader of a party with roots in post-fascist politics, broke that pattern and became one of Europe's most stable leaders. In March 2026 she suffered her first real defeat, and it came from the voters directly.

On 22 and 23 March, Italians voted on a constitutional reform of the judiciary, the government's flagship pledge, which would have separated the careers of judges and prosecutors and reshaped the body that disciplines them. Meloni's camp said it would modernise a justice system where a civil case takes seven years on average; the magistrates and the opposition said it could put prosecutors under political control. The "No" side won with 53.7 percent, on a record referendum turnout of nearly 59 percent (ANSA). It carried almost every region except the northern strongholds of Veneto, Lombardy and Friuli. Meloni accepted the result, called it a "missed opportunity to modernise Italy," and said her government would go on; former prime minister Matteo Renzi, who resigned after losing his own referendum in 2016, called her a lame duck. The centre-left, led by Elly Schlein, was energised ahead of the general election due in 2027.
briefing.power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister needs the confidence of both chambers, the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate; the president, elected by parliament for seven years, appoints the prime minister and can dissolve parliament. Constitutional changes not approved by two-thirds of parliament can be put to a referendum.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni (Brothers of Italy), in office since 2022.
